tool.name: dns_hygiene_check
tool.description:
Run a battery of DNS hygiene and email-security checks on a domain target.
This tool wraps `dig` queries to evaluate the domain's posture across well-known categories: SPF, DMARC, DKIM (common selectors), MTA-STS, CAA, DNSSEC, wildcard DNS, and AXFR (zone transfer) exposure. Each misconfiguration is emitted as a structured finding via the tracer; the return value summarises every check.
Use this tool during the recon phase for any `domain` target — it produces deterministic coverage of categories the agent's free-form reasoning often misses (especially MTA-STS, DANE, CAA, AXFR which are easy to overlook).
Categories the findings file under: `email_security` (SPF, DMARC, MTA-STS), `dns_security` (CAA, DNSSEC, wildcard, AXFR).
Returns a dict: `{success, domain, checks_run, results: [...], findings_emitted}`. Each entry in `results` describes one check's outcome; the side-effect findings carry the full description / impact / remediation.

parameter.name: domain
parameter.description: Domain to check (apex, e.g. "example.com" — not a URL, not a subdomain unless that's the apex of interest).

parameter.name: checks
parameter.description: Comma-separated list of checks to run, e.g. "spf,dmarc,caa". Default is "all". Valid values: spf, dmarc, dkim, mta_sts, caa, dnssec, wildcard, axfr.

returns.description: {success, domain, checks_run, results, findings_emitted}. Findings are written through the tracer side-effect; the agent does not need to re-emit them.
